issues.legal_issue: A deed securing repayment of a debt by an interest in land creates a mortgage rather than a lease when the parties’ intention and the transaction’s terms establish a debtor-creditor relationship and the land is security for repayment.
material_facts: The executant was indebted to the other party, and the deed arranged for the debt to be repaid after a specified term.
The deed expressly made the land interest security for the amount payable and described the transaction in several places as a mortgage.
The other party was to receive income from the land and apply it towards interest, while the executant retained an obligation to repay the principal.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was a mortgage, not a lease.
issues.legal_principle: The parties’ intention, discerned from the deed as a whole, governs its construction. Where there is a debt and land is given as security for its repayment, the transaction is a mortgage whatever name the deed uses. The Court referred to Ghosh on Mortgages for this guiding rule.

predicates.redemption_suit_classifies_deed: A suit for redemption requires the court to determine whether a deed created a mortgage or a lease.
predicates.indebtedness_between_parties: One party owed money to the other party under the transaction or an existing debt arrangement.
predicates.property_secures_debt_repayment: The deed made an interest in land security for repayment of the debt.

issues.definition: When a court classifies a deed in a redemption suit and the parties’ indebtedness is secured by land, the transaction is a mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee in possession need not render accounts where the parties contracted that the entire receipts from the mortgaged property would be taken in lieu of interest, even though the mortgagee had a separate personal obligation to pay a specified amount to the mortgagor.
material_facts: The suit sought redemption and an accounting of the income received from the mortgaged property.
The deed authorized the mortgagee to take the entire income from the land and appropriate it towards interest; the mortgagor agreed not to claim the produce or any increase in it.
The mortgagee’s obligation to pay a specified amount to the mortgagor was unconditional and personal, and did not depend on the receipts or yield from the land.
The deed stated an interest rate, which the Court found was used to estimate the amount of income to be appropriated and did not contradict the parties’ clearly expressed agreement.
The Court considered that the same result followed whether the mortgage was usufructuary or anomalous.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee was not liable to render accounts to the mortgagor.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 76(g) and 76(h) of the Transfer of Property Act ordinarily require a mortgagee in possession to keep and render accounts and to apply net receipts in reduction of interest and, where appropriate, principal. Section 77 provides an exception where the parties contract that receipts from the mortgaged property are taken in lieu of interest or interest and a defined portion of principal. A specified interest rate does not by itself defeat that exception if the deed, properly construed, provides that the entire receipts are taken in lieu of interest. The Court relied on Pandit Bachchu Lal v. Chaudhri Syed Mohammad Mah, (1933) 37 C.W.N. 457. It also stated that, if the mortgage was anomalous, the contractual terms under section 98 led to the same result.

predicates.mortgage_accounting_dispute_in_redemptio: A suit for redemption disputes whether the mortgagee must account for receipts from the mortgaged property.
predicates.mortgagee_in_possession: The mortgagee took possession of the mortgaged property or received its income as mortgagee.
predicates.contract_assigns_entire_property_receipt: The parties agreed that the entire receipts from the mortgaged property would be taken in lieu of interest.
predicates.mortgagor_payment_is_personal_and_indepe: The mortgagee separately undertook to pay the mortgagor a specified amount regardless of the property’s receipts or yield.

issues.definition: In a redemption suit involving mortgage accounts, a mortgagee in possession need not render accounts if the contract assigns the entire property receipts to interest and any payment to the mortgagor is a separate personal obligation independent of those receipts.
